> “Moreover, if $X$, $S$, and $T$ are defined over a number field $F$, then $\phi$ may be taken to be defined over $F$.”

— Shinichi Mochizuki, *Noncritical Belyi Maps*, Theorem 2.5, printed pp.5–6.

Let $\overline{\mathbb Q}$ be an algebraic closure of $\mathbb Q$ and $\Omega$ an algebraic closure of $\mathbb Q(t)$. A model of index $N\in\mathbb N$ is an intermediate field $F$ of $\Omega/\mathbb Q$ with $u,v\in F$ such that $u$ is transcendental over $\mathbb Q$, $u^N+v^N=1$, $F=\mathbb Q(u,v)$, and $F/\mathbb Q(u)$ is finite dimensional of dimension $N$. If $N=0$, the model equation would give $2=1$, so no such model exists. A place $P$ is a proper valuation subring $O_P\subsetneq F$ containing all rationals, with residue field $\kappa_P$. Discreteness means every $O_P$ is a discrete valuation ring; finite residues means every $\kappa_P$ is finite dimensional over $\mathbb Q$. Under discreteness, $o_P(f)$ denotes minus the total logarithm of the maximal-ideal valuation of $f$ used in the code, including $o_P(0)=0$; put $m_P(f)=\max(0,-o_P(f))$. Set $e_P(f)=o_P(\operatorname{minpoly}_{\mathbb Q}( ar f)(f))$ if $f\in O_P$, with $ ar f$ its residue, and $e_P(f)=-o_P(f)$ otherwise. Put $S_f=\{P:o_P(f)
e0	ext{ or }o_P(f-1)>0\}$. The Belyi condition means exactly that $f$ is transcendental over $\mathbb Q$ and $e_P(f)>1$ implies $P\in S_f$ at every place. A divisor is a finitely supported integer-valued function on places, with $\deg D=\sum_P D(P)[\kappa_P:\mathbb Q]$. A polar presentation $R=(f,g)$ of $D$ means $D(P)=m_P(f)-m_P(g)$ for every $P$, without requiring $f,g
e0$. Canonical data are a divisor $D_K$ whose coefficient is $e_P(u)-1$ if $u\in O_P$ and $-e_P(u)-1$ otherwise. Infinity data are a divisor $D_H$ with coefficient $\max(m_P(u),m_P(v))$. Adjunction data are a nonzero $r\in F$ with $D_K(P)=(N-3)D_H(P)+o_P(r)$ everywhere; subtraction here is in the integers. For finite $S_\phi$, let $E_\phi=\sum_{P\in S_\phi}P$. Generator data are a finite set $G\subset F$ containing $\phi,\phi^{-1},(1-\phi)^{-1}$, such that its generated $\mathbb Q$-subalgebra equals $\{f\in F:f\in O_P	ext{ for all }P
otin S_\phi\}$. An arithmetic choice package consists of canonical data, infinity data, adjunction data for them, a polar presentation of $D_K$, a polar presentation of $E_\phi$, and generator data. An algebraic-closure-valued point $x$ is a place $P_x$ and ring homomorphism $\sigma_x:\kappa_{P_x}	o\overline{\mathbb Q}$. For $f\in O_{P_x}$, $x(f)$ is its residue mapped by $\sigma_x$. Its field $k_x$ is the image of $\sigma_x$ and its degree is $[k_x:\mathbb Q]$, using natural-number vector-space dimension, which returns zero for infinite-dimensional extensions. An affine identification $A$ is a bijection between these points satisfying $u,v\in O_{P_x}$ and $x(u),x(v)
e0$ and the pairs $p=(a,b)\in\overline{\mathbb Q}^{,2}$ with $a^N+b^N=1$ and $a,b
e0$, preserving both coordinate evaluations and satisfying $k_x=\mathbb Q(a,b)$. Write $x_p$ for the inverse image, $L_p=\mathbb Q(a,b)$, and $d_p=[L_p:\mathbb Q]$. A good value of $\phi$ at $x$ means $\phi\in O_{P_x}$ and $x(\phi)
e0,1$. The image $z_\phi(x)$ equals $x(\phi)$ in this case and equals the rational number $2$ otherwise. For an algebraic number $z$, let $d_z=[\mathbb Q(z):\mathbb Q]$ and $h(z)=\operatorname{logHeight}_1(z	ext{ in }\mathbb Q(z))/d_z$, with the height library's logarithmic height. For $R=(f,g)$, define $h_R(x)=H_f(x)-H_g(x)$, where $H_f(x)=h(x(f))$ if $f\in O_{P_x}$ and is zero otherwise: poles contribute zero, and a regular zero also has height zero. Put $h_N(p)=(N-3)\operatorname{logHeight}([a:b:1]	ext{ over }L_p)/d_p$, taking $N-3$ in the reals. For $z
e0,1$, put $\Delta(z)=\log|\operatorname{disc}\mathbb Q(z)|/d_z$ and $c(z)=d_z^{-1}\sum_w\log\operatorname N\mathfrak p_w$, summing over finite places of $\mathbb Q(z)$ with $w(z)
e1$ or $w(z-1)
e1$; $\operatorname N$ is absolute ideal norm. Put $\Delta_N(p)=\log|\operatorname{disc}L_p|/d_p$. For finite $G\subset F$, $c_G(x)=0$ if any $g\in G$ is outside $O_{P_x}$; otherwise it is $[k_x:\mathbb Q]^{-1}$ times the finite-support sum of $\log\operatorname N\mathfrak p_w$ over finite places $w$ of $k_x$ for which some $g\in G$ has $w(x(g))>1$. Thus this generator test is $>1$. The finite-support sum is zero for infinite support, and total real division by zero is zero. Local bounds for $(x,\phi,c)$, $c\in\mathbb R$, mean a good value $z=x(\phi)$ and the inequalities $|\log\|\iota(z)\||\le c$, $|\log\|\iota(z)-1\||\le c$ for every ring homomorphism $\iota:k_x	o\mathbb C$ and every ring homomorphism $\iota:k_x	o\overline{\mathbb Q}_2$, the normed algebraic closure of the $2$-adic numbers used in the code. Local compactness means that for each $d\in\mathbb N$ and sequence $(x_n)$ with $[k_{x_n}:\mathbb Q]\le d$, some strictly increasing $s:\mathbb N	o\mathbb N$ and finite set of places $T$ have the following property: each $\phi
e0,1$ with $\phi,\phi^{-1},(\phi-1)^{-1}\in O_P$ for every $P\in T$ admits a real $c$ giving local bounds at $x_{s(n)}$ for all sufficiently large $n$. Avoidance regularity means, for every $\phi,P$, that $P
otin S_\phi$ implies those three memberships. Noncritical selection means that for every finite $T$ a function satisfying the Belyi condition exists with $S_\phi\cap T=\varnothing$. A compact bound $(V,b)$ consists of a finite set $V$ of rational primes containing $2$ and an arbitrary real $b$; its set comprises $z\in\overline{\mathbb Q}\setminus\{0,1\}$ with $|\log w(z)|,|\log w(z-1)|\le b$ at every finite place of $\mathbb Q(z)$ whose residue characteristic lies in $V$, and at every infinite place. The embedding-to-set assumption says that, for all $x,\phi,d,c$, degree at most $d$ and local bounds imply $z_\phi(x)$ belongs to this set for $V=\{2\}$ and $b=(d+1)\max(c,0)$. Assume six propositions with the following exact scopes. First, for every model with $N>3$, discreteness and finite residues, and every canonical, infinity and adjunction datum, $\deg D_K=N(N-3)$. Second, for all those data, each affine identification and each polar presentation $R_K$, a real constant uniformly bounds $|h_{R_K}(x_p)-h_N(p)|$ for all pairs $p$. Third, for every natural $N$, model with discreteness and finite residues, affine identification, function satisfying the Belyi condition, proof of finite cusp set and arithmetic package $B$, a real constant uniformly bounds $|h_{R_K}(x_p)+h_{R_E}(x_p)-h(z_\phi(x_p))|$ for all $p$ with good value, using the presentations in $B$. Fourth, for every natural $N$, model with discreteness and finite residues, divisors $D,E$, arbitrary polar presentations $R_D,R_E$, and real $q$ with $\deg D>0$ and $\deg E<q\deg D$, a real $C$ satisfies $h_{R_E}(x)\le qh_{R_D}(x)+C$ for every algebraic-closure-valued point $x$. Fifth, for every natural $N$, model with discreteness and finite residues, affine identification, function satisfying the Belyi condition, proof of finite cusp set and generator datum $G$, a real $C$ satisfies $\Delta(z_\phi(x_p))+c(z_\phi(x_p))\le\Delta_N(p)+c_G(x_p)+C$ for all $p$ with good value. Sixth, for all data in the fifth proposition and each polar presentation $R_E$ of $E_\phi$, a real $C$ satisfies $c_G(x_p)\le h_{R_E}(x_p)+C$ for all $p$ with good value. Each constant is chosen after the indicated data, may depend on them, and is uniform in the indicated points. In addition to these six propositions assume the following five statements: for every $N>3$, there exist a model, discreteness, finite residues, an affine identification, noncritical selection and finiteness of $S_\phi$ for every function satisfying the Belyi condition; every model with discreteness and finite residues has local compactness; every model with any discreteness has avoidance regularity, without a finite-residue assumption; every model with finite residues has the embedding-to-set property; and for every $N>3$, model with discreteness and finite residues, function satisfying the Belyi condition and proof of finite cusp set, an arithmetic choice package exists. Then the following implication holds: if, for every $d\in\mathbb N$, real $\eta>0$ and compact bound $(V,b)$, there exists $C\in\mathbb R$ such that $h(z)\le(1+\eta)(\Delta(z)+c(z))+C$ for every $z$ in its specified set with $d_z\le d$, then for every $N>3$, $d\in\mathbb N$ and real $\varepsilon>0$, there exists $C\in\mathbb R$ such that $h_N(p)\le(1+\varepsilon)\Delta_N(p)+C$ for every pair $p=(a,b)$ with $a^N+b^N=1$, $a,b
e0$ and $d_p\le d$. The conclusion has no compact-set restriction on $p$. Its constant is uniform in $p$ after $N,d,\varepsilon$ are fixed; the antecedent allows dependence on the compact bound. The case $d=0$ is included and the pointwise conclusions there are vacuous, since these number-field degrees are positive. All eleven assumptions above, including the six comparison propositions, are hypotheses of this theorem.

otin S_\phi	ext{ で成立}\}$ に等しいものである。算術的選択の組は標準因子データ、無限遠因子データ、それらの随伴データ、$D_K$ の極表示、$E_\phi$ の極表示、および生成元データからなる。 代数閉包に値をもつ点 $x$ は、素点 $P_x$ と環準同型 $\sigma_x:\kappa_{P_x}	o\overline{\mathbb Q}$ の組である。$f\in O_{P_x}$ に対する $x(f)$ は剰余類の $\sigma_x$ による像である。点の体 $k_x$ は $\sigma_x$ の像、次数は $[k_x:\mathbb Q]$ であり、無限次元拡大では零を返す自然数値のベクトル空間次元を用いる。アフィン同定 $A$ は、$u,v\in O_{P_x}$ かつ $x(u),x(v)
e0$ を満たすこれらの点と、$a^N+b^N=1$ かつ $a,b
e0$ を満たす組 $p=(a,b)\in\overline{\mathbb Q}^{,2}$ との全単射で、両座標の評価を保存し、$k_x=\mathbb Q(a,b)$ を満たす。逆像を $x_p$ と書き、$L_p=\mathbb Q(a,b)$、$d_p=[L_p:\mathbb Q]$ と置く。$\phi$ が $x$ で良い値をもつとは $\phi\in O_{P_x}$ かつ $x(\phi)
e0,1$ であることをいう。像 $z_\phi(x)$ はこの場合 $x(\phi)$、それ以外では有理数 $2$ である。 代数的数 $z$ に対して $d_z=[\mathbb Q(z):\mathbb Q]$、$h(z)=\operatorname{logHeight}_1(z	ext{ を }\mathbb Q(z)	ext{ の元としたもの})/d_z$ とし、高さライブラリの対数的高さを用いる。$R=(f,g)$ に対し $h_R(x)=H_f(x)-H_g(x)$ とする。ただし $f\in O_{P_x}$ なら $H_f(x)=h(x(f))$、それ以外では零とする。したがって極での寄与は零で、正則な零値の高さも零である。$h_N(p)=(N-3)\operatorname{logHeight}([a:b:1]	ext{ を }L_p	ext{ 上で考えたもの})/d_p$ とし、$N-3$ は実数で計算する。 $z
e0,1$ に対し $\Delta(z)=\log|\operatorname{disc}\mathbb Q(z)|/d_z$、$c(z)=d_z^{-1}\sum_w\log\operatorname N\mathfrak p_w$ とし、和は $w(z)
e1$ または $w(z-1)
e1$ を満たす $\mathbb Q(z)$ の有限素点にわたる。$\operatorname N$ はイデアルの絶対ノルムである。$\Delta_N(p)=\log|\operatorname{disc}L_p|/d_p$ と置く。有限集合 $G\subset F$ について、ある $g\in G$ が $O_{P_x}$ に属さなければ $c_G(x)=0$ とする。それ以外では $[k_x:\mathbb Q]^{-1}$ と $\log\operatorname N\mathfrak p_w$ の有限台和との積であり、和はある $g\in G$ で $w(x(g))>1$ となる $k_x$ の有限素点にわたる。したがって生成元の判定条件は $>1$ である。台が無限なら有限台和は零で、全域的な実数除法では零による除法は零となる。 $c\in\mathbb R$ に対する $(x,\phi,c)$ の局所的有界性とは、良い値 $z=x(\phi)$ があり、すべての環準同型 $\iota:k_x	o\mathbb C$ と、コードで用いるノルム付き $2$ 進数代数閉包へのすべての環準同型 $\iota:k_x	o\overline{\mathbb Q}_2$ に対し $|\log\|\iota(z)\||\le c$、$|\log\|\iota(z)-1\||\le c$ が成立することである。局所コンパクト性とは、各 $d\in\mathbb N$ と $[k_{x_n}:\mathbb Q]\le d$ を満たす点列 $(x_n)$ に対し、狭義単調増加写像 $s:\mathbb N	o\mathbb N$ と素点の有限集合 $T$ が存在し、すべての $P\in T$ で $\phi,\phi^{-1},(\phi-1)^{-1}\in O_P$ を満たす各 $\phi
e0,1$ について、ある実数 $c$ により $x_{s(n)}$ での局所的有界性が十分大きいすべての $n$ で成立することである。回避による正則性とは、すべての $\phi,P$ で $P
otin S_\phi$ ならこの三つの所属条件が成立することである。非臨界選択とは、各有限集合 $T$ に対し Belyi 条件と $S_\phi\cap T=\varnothing$ を満たす関数が存在することである。コンパクトな有界条件 $(V,b)$ は $2$ を含む有理素数の有限集合 $V$ と任意の実数 $b$ からなり、その集合は、剰余標数が $V$ に属する $\mathbb Q(z)$ の各有限素点と各無限素点において $|\log w(z)|,|\log w(z-1)|\le b$ を満たす $z\in\overline{\mathbb Q}\setminus\{0,1\}$ からなる。埋め込みの評価から集合への所属を得る仮定とは、すべての $x,\phi,d,c$ について、次数が $d$ 以下で局所的有界性があれば、$z_\phi(x)$ が $V=\{2\}$、$b=(d+1)\max(c,0)$ としたこの集合に属することである。 量化の範囲を次の通りとする六つの命題を仮定する。第一に、$N>3$、離散性、剰余体の有限性を満たすすべてのモデルと、すべての標準因子、無限遠因子、随伴データに対して $\deg D_K=N(N-3)$ が成立する。第二に、それらの全データ、各アフィン同定、各極表示 $R_K$ に対し、すべての組 $p$ に一様な実定数で $|h_{R_K}(x_p)-h_N(p)|$ が抑えられる。第三に、すべての自然数 $N$、離散性と剰余体の有限性を満たすモデル、アフィン同定、Belyi 条件を満たす関数、尖点集合の有限性の証明、算術的選択の組 $B$ に対し、良い値をもつすべての $p$ に一様な実定数で、$B$ 内の表示による $|h_{R_K}(x_p)+h_{R_E}(x_p)-h(z_\phi(x_p))|$ が抑えられる。第四に、すべての自然数 $N$、離散性と剰余体の有限性を満たすモデル、因子 $D,E$、任意の極表示 $R_D,R_E$、および $\deg D>0$、$\deg E<q\deg D$ を満たす実数 $q$ に対し、ある実数 $C$ によって、代数閉包に値をもつすべての点 $x$ で $h_{R_E}(x)\le qh_{R_D}(x)+C$ が成立する。第五に、すべての自然数 $N$、離散性と剰余体の有限性を満たすモデル、アフィン同定、Belyi 条件を満たす関数、尖点集合の有限性の証明、生成元データ $G$ に対し、ある実数 $C$ によって、良い値をもつすべての $p$ で $\Delta(z_\phi(x_p))+c(z_\phi(x_p))\le\Delta_N(p)+c_G(x_p)+C$ が成立する。第六に、第五項の全データと $E_\phi$ の各極表示 $R_E$ に対し、ある実数 $C$ によって、良い値をもつすべての $p$ で $c_G(x_p)\le h_{R_E}(x_p)+C$ が成立する。各定数は関連するデータの後に選び、それらに依存してよいが、対応する点には一様である。 この六つの命題に加えて次の五つを仮定する。各 $N>3$ に対してモデル、離散性、剰余体の有限性、アフィン同定、非臨界選択が存在し、Belyi 条件を満たす各関数の $S_\phi$ は有限である。離散性と剰余体の有限性を満たす各モデルには局所コンパクト性がある。任意の離散性の証明を備えた各モデルには回避による正則性があり、剰余体の有限性は要求しない。剰余体が有限次の各モデルには埋め込みの評価から集合への所属を得る性質がある。各 $N>3$、離散性と剰余体の有限性を満たすモデル、Belyi 条件を満たす関数、および尖点集合の有限性の証明に対して算術的選択の組が存在する。このとき次の含意が成立する。任意の $d\in\mathbb N$、実数 $\eta>0$、コンパクトな有界条件 $(V,b)$ に対して、ある $C\in\mathbb R$ が存在し、その集合に属し $d_z\le d$ を満たすすべての $z$ で $h(z)\le(1+\eta)(\Delta(z)+c(z))+C$ が成立するならば、任意の $N>3$、$d\in\mathbb N$、実数 $\varepsilon>0$ に対して、ある $C\in\mathbb R$ が存在し、$a^N+b^N=1$、$a,b
e0$、$d_p\le d$ を満たすすべての組 $p=(a,b)$ で $h_N(p)\le(1+\varepsilon)\Delta_N(p)+C$ が成立する。結論には $p$ のコンパクト集合への所属条件がない。$N,d,\varepsilon$ の固定後、その定数は $p$ に一様であり、前件ではコンパクトな有界条件への依存を許す。$d=0$ も含むが、これらの数体の次数は正なので、その場合の各点に関する結論は空虚に成立する。六つの比較命題を含む上記十一の仮定はすべてこの定理の前提である。

Authors: The genl contributors

Concrete Fermat adaptation of Genl/GeneralPosition/TheoremTwoOne.lean.
All heights and conductors below are the actual definitions in the imported
modules. No real-valued function is supplied as a theorem hypothesis.
-/
import Definitions.Def_FermatBelyiComparisons

set_option autoImplicit false

namespace AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper

/-- Noncritical selection, local compactness, concrete divisor existence,
and six explicit arithmetic/height facts imply the original fixed estimate.
The actual model and its affine identity are selected from the six-node
NoncriticalInput. The proof does not assume the parent estimate as a child. -/
theorem canonicalEstimate_of_belyi_children
    (hInput : ∀ N : ℕ, 3 < N → NoncriticalInput N)
    (hCompact : ∀ {N : ℕ} (M : Model N), PlacesDiscrete M →
      ResiduesFinite M → LocalCompactness M)
    (hRegular : ∀ {N : ℕ} (M : Model N) (hDVR : PlacesDiscrete M),
      AvoidanceRegularity M hDVR)
    (hEmbedding : ∀ {N : ℕ} (M : Model N), ResiduesFinite M → EmbeddingBoundsToSet M)
    (hChoices : ∀ {N : ℕ} (M : Model N) (hDVR : PlacesDiscrete M),
      3 < N → ResiduesFinite M → ∀ (φ : M.K), IsBelyi M hDVR φ →
      ∀ hfin : (cusps M hDVR φ).Finite,
        Nonempty (ArithmeticDivisorChoices M hDVR φ hfin))
    (hDegree : CanonicalDegreeIdentity)
    (hCanonical : CanonicalHeightIdentification)
    (hHeight : BelyiHeightRelation)
    (hStrictHeight : DivisorDegreeHeightComparison)
    (hDifferent : BelyiDifferentConductorComparison)
    (hConductor : CuspConductorHeightComparison) : Fermat.CanonicalEstimate := by
  intro hII N hN d ε hε
  obtain ⟨M, hDVR, hRF, ⟨A⟩, hSelect, hFiniteCusps⟩ := hInput N hN
  have hBounded := boundedBelyiImages_of_children M hDVR A
    (hCompact M hDVR hRF) (hRegular M hDVR) hSelect (hEmbedding M hRF)
  by_contra hfail
  push_neg at hfail
  choose xs hxdeg hxfail using fun n : ℕ => hfail (n : ℝ)
  obtain ⟨φ, hφ, s, hs, K, hImages⟩ := hBounded d xs hxdeg
  have hfin := hFiniteCusps φ hφ
  obtain ⟨B⟩ := hChoices M hDVR hN hRF φ hφ hfin
  have hKdeg := hDegree M hDVR hN hRF B.canonical B.infinity B.adjunction
  have hKpos : 0 < divisorDegree M B.canonical.D := by
    rw [hKdeg]
    unfold planeCanonicalDegree
    have hNint : (3 : ℤ) < N := by exact_mod_cast hN
    nlinarith
  have hKposR : (0 : ℝ) < divisorDegree M B.canonical.D := by exact_mod_cast hKpos
  let ratio : ℝ := (divisorDegree M (cuspDivisor M hDVR φ hfin) : ℝ) /
    (planeCanonicalDegree N : ℝ)
  let q : ℝ := max ratio 0 + 1
  have hq : 0 < q := by dsimp [q]; linarith [le_max_right ratio 0]
  have hStrictQ : StrictQ M hDVR φ hfin q := by
    change ratio < q
    dsimp [q]
    linarith [le_max_left ratio 0]
  have hdegree : (divisorDegree M (cuspDivisor M hDVR φ hfin) : ℝ) <
      q * divisorDegree M B.canonical.D := by
    have hden : (0 : ℝ) < planeCanonicalDegree N := by
      rw [← hKdeg]
      exact hKposR
    have h := (div_lt_iff₀ hden).mp hStrictQ
    simpa only [hKdeg] using h
  obtain ⟨CK, hCK⟩ := hCanonical M hDVR hN hRF A
    B.canonical B.infinity B.adjunction B.canonicalPresentation
  obtain ⟨CB, hCB⟩ := hHeight M hDVR hRF A φ hφ hfin B
  obtain ⟨CQ, hCQ⟩ := hStrictHeight M hDVR hRF
    B.canonical.D (cuspDivisor M hDVR φ hfin)
    B.canonicalPresentation B.cuspPresentation q hKpos hdegree
  obtain ⟨CD, hCD⟩ := hDifferent M hDVR hRF A φ hφ hfin B.generators
  obtain ⟨CC, hCC⟩ := hConductor M hDVR hRF A φ hφ hfin
    B.generators B.cuspPresentation
  have hden : 0 < 1 + q * (1 + ε) := by nlinarith
  let δ : ℝ := ε / (1 + q * (1 + ε))
  have hδ : 0 < δ := div_pos hε hden
  have hkey : 1 + δ = (1 + ε) * (1 - δ * q) := by
    dsimp [δ]
    field_simp [hden.ne']
    <;> ring
  have hfactor : 0 < 1 - δ * q := by nlinarith
  obtain ⟨CT, hCT⟩ := hII d δ hδ K
  let C : ℝ := CT + CB + CK + (1 + δ) * (CD + CC) + δ * CQ + (δ * q) * CK
  have hchain : ∀ n : ℕ, Fermat.canonicalHeight (xs (s n)) ≤
      (1 + δ) * Fermat.logDiff (xs (s n)) +
        (δ * q) * Fermat.canonicalHeight (xs (s n)) + C := by
    intro n
    obtain ⟨hgood, hmem, hd⟩ := hImages n
    have ht := hCT (belyiImage M φ (affineLift M A (xs (s n)))) hmem hd
    have hk := abs_le.mp (hCK (xs (s n)))
    have hb := abs_le.mp (hCB (xs (s n)) hgood)
    have hd := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (hCD (xs (s n)) hgood)
      (by linarith : 0 ≤ 1 + δ)
    have hc := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (hCC (xs (s n)) hgood)
      (by linarith : 0 ≤ 1 + δ)
    have he := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (hCQ (affineLift M A (xs (s n)))) hδ.le
    have hkupper : divHeight B.canonicalPresentation (affineLift M A (xs (s n))) ≤
        Fermat.canonicalHeight (xs (s n)) + CK := by linarith [hk.2]
    have hkq := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hkupper (mul_nonneg hδ.le hq.le)
    dsimp [C]
    nlinarith [hk.1, hk.2, hb.1, hb.2]
  obtain ⟨n, hn⟩ := exists_nat_gt (C / (1 - δ * q))
  have hsn : C / (1 - δ * q) < (s n : ℝ) :=
    hn.trans_le (by exact_mod_cast hs.id_le n)
  have hlarge : C < (1 - δ * q) * (s n : ℝ) := by
    have h := mul_lt_mul_of_pos_left hsn hfactor
    rwa [mul_div_cancel₀ _ hfactor.ne'] at h
  have hfailn := mul_lt_mul_of_pos_left (hxfail (s n)) hfactor
  have hbound := hchain n
  rw [hkey] at hbound
  nlinarith

end AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper
source: Shinichi Mochizuki, Arithmetic Elliptic Curves in General Position, Propositions 1.4, 1.6, 1.7 and Theorem 2.1, printed pp.11–13; https://www.kurims.kyoto-u.ac.jp/~motizuki/Arithmetic%20Elliptic%20Curves%20in%20General%20Position.pdf . Shinichi Mochizuki, Noncritical Belyi Maps, Theorem 2.5 and Corollary 3.2, pp.5–8; https://www.kurims.kyoto-u.ac.jp/~motizuki/Noncritical%20Belyi%20Maps.pdf . Independent concrete Fermat adaptation of Belyi 9ce4d3f793d3bc831f2fc7214b7dbad90ea012d8, Heights 721496ca4c158e511d25d8ccf6bfe8503eda73c1, and Genl ea2846c877d1e16d8f0b911a5fed07f5ee69eaaf. No Iut/Genl/Heights/Belyi runtime import is used. Source numerical contradiction Genl/GeneralPosition/TheoremTwoOne.lean:59–126. Apply local compactness to the entire bounded-degree failure sequence, choose a genuine noncritical Belyi map and actual divisor/coordinate-ring data, and use delta=epsilon/(1+q*(1+epsilon)) for a strict q above the actual cusp/canonical degree ratio. Strictly increasing subsequence indices preserve unbounded failure. This is a conditional combination of exactly twenty Open children.
